name: Solvang Drift Parka
description:
Solvang is a Scandinavian-heritage outdoor brand that's been operating in the Great Lakes corridor for decades, selling gear to people who actually spend time outside in the region's serious winters. The Drift Parka is their cold-weather workhorse — a mid-thigh length shell in a matte ripstop with a down-analog synthetic fill, the hood oversized enough to accommodate a helmet or a heavy hat and still close around the face. The design is deliberately understated: two colors, glacier white and a dark navy, no visible branding beyond a small embossed logo at the chest zip. The insulation runs to the wrists and the fill weight is serious enough that below-zero temperatures feel like a negotiation rather than a defeat.

This is a Tier 3 to Tier 4 purchase — expensive enough that Tier 2 buyers make it a significant investment, cheap enough that it's not a status item in the Spire. Wilderness guides, researchers who work at the lake-monitoring stations, and people who commute via elevated walkways in January all wear it. It has none of the tech features of its more expensive competitors and doesn't need them. It is simply a very good parka.
what_it_says: You respect the weather. You've been outside when it got serious.
worn_by: Tier 4 buyers who want function over status
story_hooks: A researcher found something at the lake monitoring station she wasn't supposed to find, and the only record of her being there is a glacier-white parka on a security camera she didn't know about.
The Solvang warehouse doubles as a meeting point for a mutual aid network that operates in the outer Tier 2 zones; the parka has become an informal identifier.
A Tier 4 buyer paid resale for a parka that still has the previous owner's name written in marker on the interior tag — a name that appears on a missing persons list.

physical_description.visual_profile: A austere, purposeful silhouette that reads "function over form." The Drift Parka hangs straight from the shoulders, hitting mid-thigh with a subtle A-line from the torso. The oversized hood creates a rounded, protective frame that dominates the upper half when drawn. The overall impression is solid, reliable, and deeply utilitarian—the kind of garment that disappears into someone's daily life rather than announcing itself.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with tapered wrists; designed to layer without restriction. The hood fits generously around the head and neck, accommodating augmentation ports, heavy insulation, or a climate-sealed helmet. Armholes sit slightly dropped to allow free shoulder movement in complex urban climbing or traversal.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte ripstop polyester shell with a subtle grid weave visible only up close. Down-analog synthetic fill (likely algae-derived or lab-cultured protein matrix) rated for extreme cold retention without animal products.
physical_description.texture: The shell has a soft, non-reflective matte finish that resists gloss and radar signature. Micro-ripples across the surface create subtle depth. The fill adds gentle quilting visible as diagonal stitching patterns that stabilize the insulation without creating bulk.
physical_description.color_scheme: Glacier white as primary (Solvang's signature) or dark navy as alternative. Both are deliberately desaturated—no vibrant branding colors. The combination reads 'winter landscape' rather than 'fashion statement.' Small embossed logo at chest zip in tonal color matching.
physical_description.closures: Full-length YKK or equivalent heavy-duty two-way slider zipper with a storm flap. Drawstring hood with friction-fit adjusters. Elastic cuffs at wrists; no additional buckles or fasteners.
distinctive_features: Oversized hood engineered to fit over helmet or augmentation crown
Insulation extends to the knuckles—no exposed wrist on the interior
Subtle internal quilting grid visible only when worn
Minimal branding: single embossed chest logo, no visible text
Matte finish deliberately avoids reflectivity in low-light urban environments
Two-way slider allows venting from bottom or top independently
Reinforced stress points at shoulders and sleeve seams
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 boundary. Expensive enough to signal stability and investment in quality, but not conspicuous wealth. A Tier 2 corpo might wear it as genuine outerwear for fieldwork; a Tier 4 worker wears it as their best jacket.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by wilderness guides, environmental researchers at Great Lakes monitoring stations, climbers using elevated walkway networks in winter, and anyone who spends serious time outside in subzero conditions. Signals 'I actually work outdoors' or 'I take cold weather seriously' rather than 'I can afford status gear.' Associated with Scandinavian pragmatism and Great Lakes regional identity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly broken-in. These parkas age beautifully—matte surface develops character through use but doesn't show stains obviously. A well-worn Drift Parka might have slightly softened edges or faint salt stains from lake-effect snow, but the construction is robust enough that it looks 'seasoned' rather than 'damaged.'

image_prompt: Neo-noir fashion photography: Solvang Drift Parka in glacier white on a androgynous model with visible subcutaneous bioluminescent port tracery at the neck, standing in profile against a Great Lakes industrial backdrop at dusk. Hood drawn up, small embossed logo visible at chest, matte ripstop surface catching cold blue-grey light. Elevated walkway and frost-rimed guardrail visible behind.
